text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any pain or burning when you urinate, and have you noticed any fever or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Iron deficiency anemia does not cause fever, uterine tenderness, or decreased bowel sounds, so that previous assessment was incorrect. I suspect endometritis, possibly complicated by pelvic abscess given the decreased bowel sounds. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, C-Reactive Protein, Pelvic Ultrasound
